findings.costIfIgnored: Complaints and loss of trust if customers feel data use was unclear, plus questions from the regulator and possible pause by the payment helper.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a lawful basis note for sign up, booking storage and Paystack sharing, show it in the sign up and booking flow, and store consent or contract record with timestamp.
findings.plain: Check this: The sign up page collects name, phone, email and secret word for log in and the booking flow stores service, date and time against the account and shares email and amount with Paystack to take the deposit. This may touch the law duty that Personal data may only be processed where the person has given, and not withdrawn, consent for the specific purpose, or where the processing is necessary for a listed reason such as performing a contract with the person, meeting a legal obligation, or a legitimate interest that does not override the person's rights. Evidence found in code. Please check and record the lawful basis for each use and what to show the customer. This is not legal advice and the owner should confirm with a qualified adviser.
findings.title: Check this: Lawful basis for account and booking data and Paystack sharing

findings.costIfIgnored: Customers may complain about old data kept forever and trust may fall if deletion requests cannot be met.
findings.fixPrompt: Set a retention period for accounts and bookings, add a job to delete or anonymise old records, and document what happens on cancel and on account close.
findings.plain: Check this: Cancel keeps the booking as cancelled and the app shows no delete for accounts and no timetable for removal of old bookings. This may touch the law duty that Personal data must be kept for no longer than is necessary to achieve the lawful basis for which it was collected. Evidence found in code. Please check what retention period fits the booking need and add removal or anonymisation. This is not legal advice and the owner should confirm with a qualified adviser.
findings.title: Check this: How long bookings and accounts are kept

findings.costIfIgnored: Customers may not understand use of data and may complain, and trust may be lost if purposes and contacts are hidden.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a clear privacy notice link on the sign up and booking sections, name Paystack and other recipients, state purposes, rights, retention and complaint contact, and keep wording simple.
findings.plain: Check this: The sign up form asks for name, phone, email and secret word and shows no privacy policy link in the visible form. This may touch the law duty that Before collecting personal data directly from a person, the business must tell them who it is and how to contact it, the lawful basis and purposes, who receives the data, their rights, the retention period, their right to complain to the Commission, and any automated decision making. Gap in code. Please check and add a clear and easily reached privacy notice before collection. This is not legal advice and the owner should confirm with a qualified adviser.
findings.title: Check this: Privacy notice before sign up

findings.costIfIgnored: Frustrated customers and loss of trust if people cannot see what is held about them or get a copy.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a My data page or request route where a logged in customer can see account plus booking data, purposes, recipients and retention, and can download a copy in a common format.
findings.plain: Check this: Logged in customers can see own bookings with service, date, time, status and amount paid but there is no download copy or clear request route for all data held. This may touch the law duty that A person can ask the business, without constraint or unreasonable delay, to confirm whether it holds their personal data and, if so, to be told among other things the purposes, categories, recipients and, where possible, the retention period or the criteria used to set it. Evidence found in code. Please check how a customer can ask for confirmation and get a copy in a commonly used electronic format. This is not legal advice and the owner should confirm with a qualified adviser.
findings.title: Check this: Customer access to own data and copy

findings.costIfIgnored: Complaints if wrong contact details cannot be fixed and if delete requests leave personal data behind.
findings.fixPrompt: Add edit for name, phone and email, add delete account request, and make delete remove or anonymise personal data in users and bookings without undue delay.
findings.plain: Check this: Customers can view own bookings and cancel own booking but there is no edit for name, phone or email and no delete account choice in the described flows. This may touch the law duty that A person can have inaccurate, out of date, incomplete or misleading data corrected, and can have their personal data erased without undue delay. Evidence found in described flow plus Gap for edit and delete. Please check how to allow correction and erasure without undue delay. This is not legal advice and the owner should confirm with a qualified adviser.
findings.quote: Flow: Logged in customer opens My bookings to see service, date, time, status and amount paid, and can cancel own booking
findings.title: Check this: Correction and deletion of account and booking data

findings.costIfIgnored: Slow response and loss of trust if an incident is missed, plus questions from the regulator and affected people left unsure how to protect themselves.
findings.fixPrompt: Add basic access logging and alerts for customer data, name an incident contact, write steps to assess and record incidents and to notify where needed, and keep an incident log.
findings.plain: Check this: The app stores account names, phones, emails and booking history with timestamps and shows no incident log, alert or contact plan in the files shown. This may touch the law duty for reporting a personal data incident within 72 hours where there is risk to people, telling affected people in plain language where risk is high, and keeping a record of facts, effects and action taken. No evidence in code for logging or plan. Please check what logging, contacts and records are needed. This is not legal advice and the owner should confirm with a qualified adviser.
findings.title: Check this: Plan for reporting a personal data incident

findings.costIfIgnored: Unclear responsibility if a helper mishandles data, leading to complaints and loss of trust.
findings.fixPrompt: List Paystack and any hosting or messaging helper that handles personal data, review their data terms, and store the written agreement reference for each.
findings.plain: Check this: The booking flow sends email, amount and reference to Paystack for verification and stores data in the app database. This may touch the law duty that When the business uses another party to process personal data on its behalf, it must make sure that party follows the Act, helps it honour people's rights, keeps the data secure, and gives information needed to show compliance. This includes a written agreement. Evidence found in code. Please check the written terms with Paystack and any hosting or messaging helper. This is not legal advice and the owner should confirm with a qualified adviser.
findings.title: Check this: Written terms with Paystack and other helpers

findings.costIfIgnored: Higher risk of script theft on the payment page and possible loss of payment provider support and customer trust.
findings.fixPrompt: Confirm Paystack inline use as instructed, inventory scripts on the booking page, remove unneeded third party scripts, and enable script integrity and monitoring as provider guides.
findings.plain: Check this: The home page loads the Paystack inline script and the booking flow opens the Paystack popup inside the site to collect the deposit. This may touch the standard duty in SAQ A r1 eligibility criterion for scripts (PCI DSS v4.0.1), with Requirements 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 as example techniques to confirm the page is not open to script attacks. Evidence found in code. Please check provider guidance and confirm protection or use of redirect as instructed. This is a standard, not law, and this is not legal advice and the owner should confirm with a qualified adviser.
findings.title: Check this: Protection for page that shows Paystack payment popup
